newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 6.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 6.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MEDIA

WALLDORF - Sales of magazines and newspapers in Germany are down, say press wholesalers at their conference in Baden-Baden. First-quarter sales dropped five percent in the western German states, and wholesalers expect stagnant turnover and a slight dip in sales for the rest of the year. The industry posted mild growth in turnover 1996, expanding to 6.07 billion marks ($3.5 billion) from 5.98 billion marks in 1995. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Interface Frisch und Partner advertising agency has won the seven-figure ad account of software manufacturer Symantec. (Kress)
FRANKFURT - Planet Communications of Frankfurt, formerly Ketchum and the new partner of TBWA, has won the tourism account of auto rental company Avis. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BERLIN - The trial of left-wing politician Angel Marquardt begins in a case that could further extend the growing reach of Internet law. Prosecutors have broken new ground in pursuing someone accused of leading others to "suspect" Internet pages through their own home page. The court will decide if Marquardt broke the law by putting a "hyperlink" on her home page to the Radikal magazine. (Reuter)

PARIS - French pay television company Canal Plus and Franco-German firm SECA have filed a complaint with the European Commission accusing Spain of breaching European trade rules, Canal Plus says. "By refusing to approve the decoders used by Canal Satelite Digital, the Spanish Telecommunications Market Commission has prevented the sale of decoders already marketed in other European countries...and is preventing Canal Plus and SECA from freely conducting their business as digital technology suppliers in Spain," the company says. SECA is owned in equal parts by Canal Plus and German media group Bertelsmann.

MUNICH - The German unit of Internet search engine company Yahoo has signed a deal with U.S. online diectory service company Four11 and Meteo Consult to provide its users access to more than 13 million e-mail addresses at no additional cost, as well as current weather forecasts, Yahoo says. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Rhineland-Palatinate premier Kurt Beck says viewer fees used to support public broadcasting will not increase before the end of the year 2000. Beck, who coordinates media policy for the German states, says public network ARD will lose more than 900 million marks by the end of the year 2000. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

BERLIN - Axel Springer publishing house says it expects significantly better results for 1997. Annual profits climbed in 1996 to 164 million marks from 142 million marks in the previous year. Turnover grew to 4,420 billion marks from 4,146 billion marks during 1995. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - The long-awaited turnaround in Germany's job market is still nowhere to be seen with May numbers due to disappoint and Finance Minister Theo Waigel admitting the economy was no great help. The continuing jobs slump comes as Germany courts increasing unpopularity in Europe with its continued opposition to a European Union employment chapter, a stance that could yet lead to political risks for Chancellor Helmut Kohl at home. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Siemens AG chief executive Heinrich von Pierer says the company had no plans to leave the nuclear energy business in the foreseeable future, despite some public opposition to the technology in Germany. The world's increasing population is quickly raising demand for energy, he says at a celebration of the company's 150th birthday. (Reuter)

STUTTGART - Ford-Werke AG, the German unit of U.S. carmaker Ford Motor Co, says it aims to break even this year after reporting a loss of 551.6 million marks in 1996. The company aims to hold sales steady and reach "a neutral result" in 1997, supervisory board chairman Albert Caspers says at the opening of a new Ford branch in Stuttgart. "We hope that we will end at break-even," Caspers says. (Reuter)

STUTTGART - Prosecutors say they are investigating a senior executive of Daimler-Benz AG for allegedly infringing rules on the disclosure of earnings. The probe refers to remarks made at the Geneva auto show by management board member Eckard Cordes, who told reporters Daimler's group 1996 net profit would be more than 2 billion marks and sales would total around 107 billion marks. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Apple Computer Inc says it wants to return to profitability by the end of September under a structure based on annual sales of about $7.5 billion. The company is in the process of eliminating 4,000 jobs to streamline operations and bring it into the black, executive vice president Guerrino De Luca says. (Reuter)

BERLIN - The German computer industry expects robust growth again this year after strong expansion in 1996, an industry association says. The industry posted five percent growth in service, hardware and software turnover for 1996 to 80.5 billion marks, and foresees another six percent climb for the current year, says the chairman of the German computer industry association, Joerg Menno Harms. (Reuter)

BONN - Industrial orders grew 3.3 percent in April from the preceding month, the Economics Ministry says, an unusually strong gain compared with a 0.9 percent rise in March. Orders were up 6.2 percent from the year-earlier month, after a 5.5 percent annual gain in March. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Dr. Manfred May has been named general manager of the Axel Springer Company for Journalism. He previously held the post between 1987 and 1995. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Oliver Heieck, press spokesman of Nike Deutschland, has left the company. Nike has not yet found a replacement. (Kress)
